hook.text: Traditional security trusts everything inside the network. Zero trust says: never trust, always verify.

buildup.text: Every request is authenticated and authorized, whether it comes from inside or outside the network.

discovery.text: Access is granted per resource, per session. You prove your identity and device health every single time.

twist.text: Zero trust doesn't eliminate firewalls — it adds identity verification everywhere. Defense in depth, not replacement.

climax.text: Google's BeyondCorp was an early zero-trust system. Employees access apps based on identity, not network location.

punchline.text: Zero trust: the network location is not a security credential.

quiz.question: What is the core principle of zero trust?
options: Never trust, always verify — regardless of network location
Trust all devices inside the corporate firewall

details.summary: Zero trust assumes no user, device, or network is inherently trustworthy and verifies every access request regardless of location. It replaces the perimeter-based model where everything inside the network was trusted.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional perimeter security fails when attackers get inside the network or when users work remotely. Zero trust provides security that works regardless of where users and resources are located.
takeaways: Never trust, always verify — every request is authenticated
Access decisions consider identity, device, location, and behavior
Micro-segmentation limits access to only required resources

faq.question: How does zero trust differ from VPN-based security?
faq.answer: VPNs grant broad network access once connected, trusting the user after initial authentication. Zero trust grants access to specific applications only, continuously verifying identity, device health, and behavior for each request.

faq.question: How do you implement zero trust?
faq.answer: Start with strong identity verification and MFA for all users. Implement device health checks before granting access. Apply micro-segmentation and least-privilege policies. Monitor and log all access for anomaly detection. Use identity-aware proxies for application access.
